newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 20.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on its front page on May 20:
WASHINGTON - Maryland Gov. Parris Glendening ordered an advanced automobile emissions test to become mandatory for most state motorists on Oct. 1.
WASHINGTON - The American Medical Assocation endorsed a bill to restrict "partial birth" abortions just as the legislation faces a tight vote in the Senate.
WASHINGTON - Police officials are focusing more on fighting crime and less on answering 911 calls.
WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton said he will renew China's trading privileges despite its human rights abuses, opening what promises to be a fractious fight in Congress.

DENVER - An FBI chemist testified that explosive residue was found on the clothing and personal effects taken from Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh when he was arrested an hour and a half after the explosion.
WASHINGTON - Tiger Woods has rapidly become golf's reigning superstar, and now he is rivalling Michael Jordan as the most salable man in America.
